## Context
While validating the duration-probe change for similar-operose-alligator, an unchanged-tree full-suite rerun completed all 16,691 tests but produced two teardown errors. In both cases the autouse repository-isolation guard reached tests/conftest.py::_no_repo_commits after the test body passed, then tests/_isolation.py::head timed out its read-only git -C <worktree> rev-parse HEAD child at the fixed five-second watchdog. The failing nodes were test_snapshot_cache_by_sha and one test_registry_lane_transient_failures parameter. A prior unchanged-tree run passed completely.

Closed bug callous-amused-hart introduced the five-second watchdog after measuring 100 unloaded probes at median 0.0143s, p95 0.0164s, max 0.0610s. That calibration did not measure the guard under the full-suite concurrent workload. The present root cause is not yet known: live candidates include host/process-spawn saturation, Git/object-store contention, inherited test state, or an incorrectly calibrated watchdog.

## Plan
- Reproduce and quantify head() probe latency sequentially and under controlled concurrency matching the suite worker/process load.
- Capture runtime process/stack state for a slow probe and distinguish Git execution, process creation/waiting, shared-repository contention, and test-state contamination.
- Compare the reported-against tree (2e890ab37f7e, base fcc740dba9b) with current origin/main and inspect history since the watchdog landed.
- Confirm or reject each falsifiable hypothesis before proposing any repair. If a product defect is proven, follow held-out RED-to-GREEN repair and reproduce the original full-suite scenario.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The failure rate and latency distribution are quantified under stated sequential and concurrent conditions.
- [x] Runtime evidence identifies the exact stage that consumes the five-second budget.
- [x] A discriminating experiment proves one root cause and rules out viable alternatives.
- [x] The ticket records defect legitimacy and origin, or an evidence-backed environment/config classification.
- [x] Any repair is proven RED then GREEN and the original full-suite scenario no longer reproduces.
